problem: Prior navigation instruction generators (LSTM/Transformer speakers) map sequences of 2D perspective features to text, ignoring 3D geometry and object semantics, and use small language decoders without broad world knowledge. General MLLMs fail zero-shot because they are trained on isolated third-person images, not egocentric trajectories.
motivation: Instruction generation supports human-robot trust, assistive navigation and progress reporting, but needs precise landmark and spatial descriptions. Human route descriptions rely on key landmarks and draft-then-refine, which suggests adding 3D BEV perception and landmark-guided refinement on top of an LLM.
key_idea: Fuse BEV features (supervised by 3D detection) with perspective features as visual prompts for a parameter-efficiently tuned LLaMA-7B, and generate instructions via landmark-draft then instruction refinement.
insight: Ablations (Table 4) show BEV features add on top of perspective features (R2R val-unseen CIDEr 0.209 fine-tuned MLLM baseline vs 0.281 with BEV alone vs 0.342 with both), and transformer fusion beats addition or concatenation (SPICE 0.208 vs 0.185/0.184). Instance-guided refinement gives a large gain (CIDEr 0.373 to 0.449) with one step, while a second step adds little. Zero-shot GPT-4V is very weak (SPICE 0.098), so task-specific tuning is needed.
method: Perspective embedding: multi-view image features are projected linearly and combined with orientation (cos/sin heading and elevation), time-step and token-type embeddings; the action view is embedded analogously.

BEV encoder: BEVFormer/BEVDepth-style deformable-attention encoder (6 blocks, 15x15 grid, ±5 m range, 4 height reference points) with a depth consistency weight (cosine similarity between predicted depth distribution and reference-point depth). It is pretrained with 3D detection supervision on Matterport3D boxes (17 categories) and then frozen.

Perspective-BEV fusion: 6 transformer layers attend BEV features against the concatenated perspective and action tokens; an 8-block query transformer with Nq=10 learnable queries compresses the output to 10 tokens per step.

Perspective-BEV prompt tuning: learnable prompts are added to the visual tokens and inserted into the top 31 layers of LLaMA-7B. Zero-init attention and learnable scale/shift vectors on linear layers are used, so added parameters are 7.2% and most of LLaMA stays frozen.

Instance-guided iterative refinement: stage 1 generates landmark (instance) tokens from observations and actions; stage 2 generates the full instruction conditioned on those landmarks; the joint objective is trained with random sampling of the two tasks, and the refinement can be repeated for multiple turns.
Instruction quality evaluation: generated instructions are used to guide HAMT/DUET on REVERIE val-unseen and to augment EDrop-follower training on R2R.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-7B (partially fine-tuned, parameter-efficient) + BEV encoder (BEVFormer-style, 3D-detection pretrained, frozen) + perspective-BEV fusion transformers
setting.training_data: R2R train (14,039 instructions) plus 6,482K PREVALENT synthetic route-instruction pairs; REVERIE train (10,466 instructions); UrbanWalk; BEV encoder pretrained with Matterport3D 3D boxes
setting.observation: multi-view egocentric RGB panoramas (K views per step) with orientation angles; BEV built from RGB
setting.action_space: not applicable (text generation; the path and actions are given as input)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth trajectory (path and actions) as input, as in the task definition; Matterport3D 3D boxes for BEV pretraining

numbers_note: Instruction-generation metrics are printed as fractions (e.g., 0.549), copied as printed. Table 7a (HAMT/DUET guided by generated instructions on REVERIE val-unseen) is HAMT SR 25.68 / SPL 22.48 and DUET SR 33.81 / SPL 23.23, not included as separate entries.
results: BEVInstructor beats the previous best speaker (Lana) on all datasets: R2R val-unseen SPICE 0.208 vs 0.194 and CIDEr 0.449 vs 0.419; REVERIE val-unseen CIDEr 0.489 vs 0.406 (val-seen 0.745 vs 0.619); UrbanWalk SPICE 0.679 vs 0.566 (Kefa-speaker). Generated instructions also improve downstream navigation guidance (HAMT/DUET) and data augmentation (EDrop-follower SR 47.1 vs 45.4), and human evaluation scores 3.64 vs 3.43 for Lana.
limitations: Instructions still lack the diversity and accuracy of human annotations; open-vocabulary settings need human filtering and correction.
No safety awareness (e.g., warnings of dangerous areas); evaluation is only in simulators with no real robot.
Requires 3D box annotations (Matterport3D) to pretrain the BEV encoder; additional refinement steps give diminishing returns.
